summaryBox.title: System Classifications
summaryBox.takeaway: Open: exchanges matter & energy; Closed: exchanges energy only; Isolated: exchanges neither.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
THERMODYNAMIC SYSTEM TYPES
                                     │
     ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                               ▼                               ▼
  OPEN SYSTEM                    CLOSED SYSTEM                   ISOLATED SYSTEM
  Exchanges BOTH matter          Exchanges ENERGY only;          Exchanges NEITHER matter

conceptBreakdown.content:
Thermodynamics evaluates energy transformations, heat-work conversions, and macro-system spontaneity across three primary system types:
• **Open System**: Exchanges both matter and energy with surroundings (e.g., open beaker of boiling water).
• **Closed System**: Exchanges energy only; matter boundary is sealed (e.g., sealed metallic cylinder).
• **Isolated System**: Exchanges neither matter nor energy with surroundings (e.g., perfect thermos flask).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.2 State Functions vs Path Functions & Property Types
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.2 State Functions vs Path Functions & Property Types
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PROPERTY CLASSIFICATION
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
  EXTENSIVE PROPERTIES                                        INTENSIVE PROPERTIES
  Depend on total mass, size, or quantity                     Independent of mass, size, or quantity
  ├── Mass (m), Volume (V)                                    ├── Temperature (T), Pressure (P), Density (d)
  ├── Mole count (n), Heat Capacity (C)                       ├── Molar Heat Capacity (C_m), Molar Volume (V_m)
  └── Internal Energy (U), Enthalpy (H),                     └── Refractive index, Surface tension, Viscosity,
      Entropy (S), Free Energy (G)                                Standard Cell Potential (E°_cell), pH
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **State Functions**: Values depend solely on the current thermodynamic state ($\oint dX = 0$). Examples: $T, P, V, U, H, S, G, A$.
• **Path Functions**: Values depend explicitly on the specific pathway taken ($\oint \delta X \neq 0$). Examples: Heat ($q$) and Work ($w$).
• **Intensive Ratio Law**: The ratio of any two extensive properties is always intensive:
$$\mathbf{\text{Molar Volume } V_m = \frac{V}{n} \quad \vert \quad \text{Density } d = \frac{m}{V} \quad \vert \quad \text{Molar Heat Capacity } C_m = \frac{C}{n}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.3 The First Law of Thermodynamics (FLOT)
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.3 The First Law of Thermodynamics (FLOT)
conceptBreakdown.content:
The First Law of Thermodynamics is energy conservation applied to thermodynamic systems:

$$\mathbf{\Delta U = q + w \quad \text{or} \quad dU = \delta q + \delta w}$$

• **IUPAC Sign Conventions**:
- Heat absorbed by system: $q > 0$ (Endothermic)
- Heat released by system: $q < 0$ (Exothermic)
- Work done ON system (Compression, $dV < 0$): $w > 0$
- Work done BY system (Expansion, $dV > 0$): $w < 0$
